text:
tara: Heads up — since ~02:12 UTC we're seeing intermittent packet loss and big p95 jumps on east-west traffic inside cluster us-west-2-gpu. Affected pods are mostly GPU inference pods using RDMA.

ricardo: Confirming. Network graphs show microbursts + retransmits between nodepool-gpu-a and nodepool-gpu-b. CPU on pods unchanged.

mike: Any change rolled recently to dual-stack or CNI?

tara: We enabled dual-stack alpha on that nodepool last week for testing (kubelet + calico IPv6). Nothing else changed.

ricardo: Did a quick tcpdump on wg-eth0 of node-23: see a bunch of ICMPv6 "Packet too big" / fragmentation-needed messages for flannel overlay v6 addresses. Example dump: 
```
06:18:13.456789 IP6 fe80::1 > fe80::2: ICMP6, packet too big, mtu=1280
06:18:13.456792 IP6 2001:db8:10::23 > 2001:db8:10::87: UDP, length 874
```

julian: mtu=1280? Our nodenet MTU should be 9000 for RDMA. Looks like the v6 path is hitting an MTU-limited tunnel or a host-side filter.

mike: RDMA (GPUDirect) breaks hard when packets fragment or get ICMPs. That would explain throughput collapse.

sre-oncall: infra-bot triggered alert: NETWORK_DEGRADATION cluster=us-west-2-gpu severity=high at 2026-03-17T02:20:00Z

infra-bot: deploy:dualstack-test promoted nodepool-gpu-alpha -> nodepool-gpu-a at 2026-03-16T22:05:12Z (user: tara) :information_source:

tara: Can someone paste `ip -6 route` + `ip link` from the host? I want to see tunnel and mtu.

ricardo: Pasting trimmed output: 
```
$ ip -6 route show
2001:db8:0:1::/64 dev cilium-host proto kernel metric 256 pref medium
fe80::/64 dev eth0 proto kernel metric 256
2001:db8:0:2::/64 via fe80::a:b dev tun0 mtu 1280
```
`ip link show tun0`: `mtu 1280 qlen 1000`

mike: so tun0 is 1280 — that's definitely our problem. Who created that tunnel? CNI?

julian: It looks like an overlay created by the cloud provider's IPv6 translation (NAT64/PLAT) for inter-node IPv6. There's a known path where the provider uses a legacy 1280 MTU over some backbone. We didn't account for it when enabling dual-stack.

tara: Workaround idea: prefer IPv4 east-west for node-to-node RDMA traffic (force kube-proxy/CNI to use v4 for intra-cluster mesh). Quick policy patch possible?

mike: We can add a node-level sysctl to drop IPv6 on the RDMA nic: `sysctl -w net.ipv6.conf.<iface>.disable_ipv6=1` but that's invasive. Better: add ip rules to prefer src IPv4 for pod traffic to other node IPs.

julian: Another option: set `net.ipv6.conf.all.mtu` higher? No — the path MTU is 1280, cannot increase. Need to avoid v6 path for large packets.

ricardo: I tested an iptables mark to route pod egress to an IPv4 route table. Quick test: mark packets >1200 and force IPv4 src? hacky but doable. Logs below from test pod: 
```
# before: iperf3 RDMA-like test
Transfer: 8.3 Gbits/sec, retransmits: 1200
# after apply rule
Transfer: 46.7 Gbits/sec, retransmits: 3
```

tara: Nice. We need a safe rollout. Proposal: 1) Apply iptables rule on canary nodepool (2 nodes) 2) Monitor RDMA perf and p95 3) If stable, roll to rest of GPU nodepools 4) Raise config with CNI vendor to add stable dual-stack RDMA-safe mode.

sre-oncall: Create incident ticket? This is impacting several production customers on Dedicated plans.

mike: Created INC-2026-412 in our tracker with initial mitigation steps (canary, rollback path, customer comm template).

julian: Also file GH-2894 for CNI vendor with packet captures showing ICMPv6 PMTU. Ask for explanation of why the overlay decreased MTU to 1280 for those segments.

tara: Quick Q — does this affect embeddings-only nodes or just RDMA?

ricardo: Mostly RDMA because large contiguous payloads are sensitive. Small RPC/embeddings unaffected except higher p95 due to retransmits.

mike: On the longer term, we should: 
- add e2e tests for dual-stack RDMA perf in CI
- add explicit IP-family routing policy in our node bootstrap
- update docs for private deployments that dual-stack may degrade RDMA unless provider supports jumbo frames for IPv6

tara: For now I'm going to pause dual-stack test promotion and roll canary rules. Doing `kubectl apply -f rdma-ipv4-prefer-daemonset.yaml --context=us-west-2`

ricardo: Applied to canary nodes. Monitoring dashboard: packet loss dropped to ~0.1% and throughput regained to baseline in 3m.

sre-oncall: Notified impacted customers with interim mitigation and ETA for fix: 6 hours.

julian: Follow-up: let's not enable auto-dualstack on any gpu nodepools until we validate provider jumbo frames for v6. Also add a preflight check in our nodepool creation flow to reject v6 if MTU < 9000.

mike: Agree. I'll open a PR to nodepool-controller to add the MTU check and auto-prefer IPv4 for RDMA labels.

tara: Thanks everyone. Please add any artifacts to INC-2026-412.

ricardo: Dropping packet captures and `ip -6 route` outputs into the incident. Also adding a short note about the cloud provider's IPv6 implementation.

infra-bot: incident INC-2026-412 status=mitigated assignee=mike eta=2026-03-17T08:00:00Z

mike: I'll coordinate the CNI vendor and provider. If anyone sees reoccurrence, ping me directly. :thumbsup:
